questions.text: Suitable reaction condition for preparation of Methyl phenyl ether is
questions.sol_text: For preparation of methyl phenyl ether (C6H5-O-CH3), Williamson's synthesis is used. This involves reaction between phenoxide ion (PhO-) and methyl halide (MeBr). PhONa provides the phenoxide ion (PhO-) and MeBr provides the methyl group. The reaction proceeds as: PhONa + MeBr → PhOCH3 + NaBr. Option (4) is correct.

questions.sol_text: The reaction sequence shows: Starting material (4-isopropyl phenol) undergoes diazotization with NaNO2/HCl to form intermediate A (diazonium salt with NO group). Treatment of A with NH4SH in H2O leads to reduction of the diazo group (-NO) to amino group (-NH2), giving compound B which is 2-amino-4-isopropyl phenol (structure 1).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: H3C - CH2 - CH - CH3 with OH group is treated with (ii) Mg, Dry ether and (iii) D2O to form product [X]. What is product [X]?
options: H3C - CH2 - C - CH3 with H and OH groups
H3C - CH2 - CH - CH3 with D group

The Grignard reagent (R-MgI) is then treated with D2O which acts as a deuterated protic source. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In the reaction, starting with a compound containing OH and COOCH3 groups on a benzene ring, it undergoes conversion to an intermediate with OH and COOH groups, which then converts to a final product with OCOCH3 and COOH groups. Identify reagents 'X' and 'Y' respectively.
questions.sol_text:
Analyzing the reaction sequence:

Starting material: Benzene ring with OH and COOCH3 groups

Step 1 (Reagent Y): Conversion to intermediate with OH and COOH
- The COOCH3 (methyl ester) group is converted to COOH (carboxylic acid)
- This is hydrolysis of the ester under acidic conditions with heat
- Reagent Y = CH3OH/H+, Δ (Fischer esterification reversal/saponification)

Step 2 (Reagent X): Conversion of intermediate to final product
- The intermediate has OH and COOH groups
- Final product has OCOCH3 (acetyl ester of phenol) and COOH groups
- The phenolic OH is acetylated to form OCOCH3
- This requires acetic anhydride in acidic medium
- Reagent X = (CH3CO)2O/H+ (acetylation of phenol)

Therefore:
- X = (CH3CO)2O/H+
- Y = CH3OH/H+, Δ

This corresponds to option (3).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A and B formed in the following set of reactions are: Starting material 1: benzene ring with OH at top and CH2OH at bottom, reacted with HBr under heat gives A. Starting material 2: benzene ring with OH at top and OCH3 at bottom, reacted with HBr under heat gives B.
options: A = benzene ring with OH and CH2Br, B = benzene ring with OH and OH
A = benzene ring with OH and CH2Br, B = benzene ring with OH and Br
A = benzene ring with Br and CH2OH, B = benzene ring with Br and Br
A = benzene ring with OH and CH2Br, B = benzene ring with OH and OCH3
questions.sol_text:
For compound A: The starting material has a benzene ring with OH (hydroxyl) group and CH2OH (primary alcohol) group. When treated with HBr under heat, the primary alcohol CH2OH undergoes SN2 substitution to form CH2Br (alkyl halide). The OH group attached to the benzene ring remains intact as it is much less reactive and the aromatic C-OH bond is strong. Product A = benzene ring with OH and CH2Br.

For compound B: The starting material has a benzene ring with OH (hydroxyl) group and OCH3 (methoxy) group. When treated with HBr under heat, the C-O bond in the methoxy group (ether linkage) undergoes cleavage due to the acidic conditions. HBr protonates the oxygen of OCH3, making it a good leaving group, and Br- attacks to displace the leaving group. This produces OH group on the benzene ring. The product B = benzene ring with OH and OH (two hydroxyl groups, one original and one formed from cleavage of methoxy group).

Therefore, the answer is option (1).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In the cumene to phenol preparation in presence of air, the intermediate is
options: Isopropyl phenyl ether (structure shown with O-C(CH3)2 group on benzene ring)
Phenyl hydroperoxide (structure shown with O-O-H group on benzene ring)
Phenyl acetate (structure shown with O-C(=O)-CH3 group on benzene ring)
Isopropylbenzene (structure shown with isopropyl group on benzene ring)
questions.sol_text:
The cumene (isopropylbenzene) to phenol preparation proceeds through the following mechanism:

1. Cumene (isopropylbenzene) reacts with oxygen (O2) in air to form an intermediate.

2. The reaction mechanism involves:
   - Oxidation of cumene by O2
   - Formation of cumene hydroperoxide intermediate: the isopropyl group is oxidized to form O-O-H (hydroperoxide) group attached to the benzene ring
   - This creates the structure shown as option (2): phenyl hydroperoxide with O-O-H substituent

3. Under acidic conditions (H+), the hydroperoxide intermediate undergoes rearrangement and cleavage:
   - The O-O bond breaks
   - Rearrangement occurs to produce phenol and acetone
   - Final products: phenol (C6H5-OH) and acetone (CH3-C(=O)-CH3)

4. The intermediate that forms between cumene and the final products (phenol and acetone) is the cumene hydroperoxide, which corresponds to structure (2) with the O-O-H group on the benzene ring.

questions.text: A solution of CrO3 in amyl alcohol has a _______ colour.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Match List-I with List-II
questions.sol_text:
The correct matches are:

A. Hoffmann Degradation → III. Br₂, NaOH
Hoffmann degradation of primary amides uses Br₂ and NaOH to produce amines with one less carbon.

B. Clemenson reduction → IV. Zn-Hg/HCl

questions.text: The correct order of pKa values for the following compounds is: (a) phenol, (b) phenol with N(CH3)2 group, (c) phenol with NO2 group, (d) phenol with isopropyl group

Explanation: The acidity of phenol is affected by substituents on the benzene ring. Electron-withdrawing groups (like NO2) increase acidity by stabilizing the phenoxide anion, resulting in lower pKa values. Electron-donating groups (like N(CH3)2 and alkyl groups) decrease acidity by destabilizing the phenoxide anion, resulting in higher pKa values. The NO2 group is a strong electron-withdrawing group (EWG), making compound (c) most acidic (lowest pKa). The unsubstituted phenol (a) has intermediate acidity. The isopropyl group is an alkyl group (EDG), making compound (d) less acidic than (a). The N(CH3)2 group is a strong electron-donating group (EDG), making compound (b) least acidic (highest pKa). Acidic strength order: c > a > d > b. Since pKa is inversely related to acidity (lower pKa = higher acidity, higher pKa = lower acidity), the order of pKa values is: b > d > a > c

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following compound will most easily be attacked by an electrophile?
questions.sol_text: Phenol is most easily attacked by an electrophile because of the presence of -OH group which increases electron density at ortho and para positions mainly. The -OH group is an activating and ortho/para directing group. It activates the benzene ring more than -CH3 group. In contrast, chlorobenzene has Cl which is electron-withdrawing (shows +R effect) and deactivates the benzene ring. Therefore, phenol is most susceptible to electrophilic aromatic substitution.

Through NaOH in alcohol (E2 elimination), it forms (B) with a vinyl group. (B) then reacts with HBr in ether (electrophilic addition) to form (C). The table shows four options for identifying (B), (C), and the relationship between (A) and (C).
questions.sol_text: From the solution provided: (A) contains a Br on benzene ring with -CHBrCH3 side chain. Upon E2 elimination with NaOH/alcohol, the Br and adjacent H are removed forming (B) with a vinyl group (C=C). When (B) reacts with HBr in ether (electrophilic addition), Br adds to the double bond forming (C) where Br is on the saturated carbon of the side chain. Since (A) and (C) both have the same molecular formula but differ in the position of Br on the benzene ring or side chain, they are position isomers. The answer is [3] - position isomers.

questions.sol_text: Reaction (2) is NOT possible. Phenol cannot be directly converted to chlorobenzene by treating with HCl. The -OH group is strongly deactivating and ortho/para directing, and direct halogenation would occur on the ring, not replacement of OH. Reactions (1), (3), and (4) are all well-established aromatic reactions: (1) Cleavage of aryl ether, (3) Nucleophilic aromatic substitution, and (4) Electrophilic aromatic substitution.

Step 2: KMnO4 further oxidizes acetic acid, breaking the C-C bond to produce formic acid (HCOOH) or methanolic acid. Step 3: NaOH, CaO with heat (soda lime process) decarboxylates the acid, removing the carboxyl group as CO2, leaving CH4 (methane) as the major product.

Treatment with HCl gives phenol (Y: C6H5OH). Phenol reacts with concentrated HNO3 under these conditions to undergo nitration at multiple positions. The OH group is strongly activating and ortho/para directing, but under concentrated HNO3 conditions, all three positions (2,4,6) get nitrated due to the strong activating effect of the OH group, forming 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid) as compound Z.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Bromination of phenol in solvent with low polarity such as CHCl3 or CS2 requires Lewis acid catalyst.
Statement II: The lewis acid catalyst polarises the bromine to generate Br+.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.sol_text: Phenol is a highly activated compound which can undergo bromination directly with Bromine without any lewis acid. Statement I is false because phenol doesn't require Lewis acid catalyst for bromination. Statement II is true because the Lewis acid catalyst does polarise bromine to generate Br+ (electrophile) when needed in less activated aromatic compounds. However, phenol is activated enough to react directly without needing this polarization.

Bromination with excess Br2/Fe on 4-nitroanisole occurs at the positions ortho to the meta-directing NO2 group and ortho to the activating OCH3 group, giving 2,6-dibromoanisole (B) with NO2 at para position.

The CHCl3 undergoes nucleophilic attack by the phenoxide, forming a dichloromethyl intermediate. The structure of this intermediate is ONa+ (phenoxide) with CHCl2 (dichloromethyl) substituent on the benzene ring. This intermediate then undergoes further rearrangement and hydrolysis to form salicylaldehyde.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which one the following compounds will readily react with dilute NaOH? (1) C6H5CH2OH (2) C2H5OH (3) (CH3)3COH (4) C6H5OH

The phenolic proton is much more acidic (pKa ≈ 10) than water. Other alcohols like aliphatic alcohols (C2H5OH, C6H5CH2OH, (CH3)3COH) do not react with dilute NaOH because their OH groups are not acidic enough - they are weaker acids than water.

B.P. ∝ M.W.

Alcohol & Phenol have intermolecular H-bonding

Statement (I): The boiling points of alcohols and phenols increase with increase in the number of C-atoms.
This is TRUE because as the number of carbon atoms increases, the molecular weight increases, and consequently the boiling point increases due to increased van der Waals forces and increased surface area for intermolecular interactions.

Statement (II): The boiling points of alcohols and phenols are higher in comparison to other class of compounds such as ethers, haloalkanes.
This is TRUE because alcohols and phenols possess intermolecular hydrogen bonding (O-H···O), which is a strong intermolecular force. In contrast, ethers and haloalkanes do not have hydrogen bonding (only dipole-dipole interactions and van der Waals forces), making their boiling points significantly lower than corresponding alcohols and phenols.

Therefore, both Statement I and Statement II are true.

The reaction is:
C6H5OH + 3Br2 → C6H2(OH)(Br)3 + 3HBr

Molar mass = 6(12) + 6(1) + 16 = 72 + 6 + 16 = 94 g/mol

From the balanced equation, 1 mole of phenol requires 3 moles of Br2

Molar mass of Br2 = 2(80) = 160 g/mol

Mass of bromine = 0.063 × 160 = 10.08 g ≈ 10.22 g

questions.text: Which one of the following, with HBr will give a phenol?
options: Benzene with CH2 group attached to a carbon with two OCH3 groups and one H

questions.sol_text:
Anisole (C6H5-O-CH3) reacts with HBr through the following mechanism:

1. Protonation: HBr protonates the oxygen of the methoxy group to form C6H5-O(+)H-CH3

2. SN2 Cleavage: Bromide ion attacks the methyl group, breaking the C-O bond:
   C6H5-O(+)H-CH3 + Br(-) → C6H5-OH + CH3Br

3. Product: Phenol (C6H5-OH) is formed along with methyl bromide (CH3Br)

This is a classic ether cleavage reaction where HBr cleaves the C-O bond of an aryl methyl ether to produce a phenol. The mechanism proceeds via SN2 attack on the activated methyl group after protonation of the oxygen.

The other options do not produce phenol:
- Option (1): Produces benzyl alcohol derivative, not phenol
- Option (3): Produces benzyl alcohol, not phenol
- Option (4): Produces a different product, not phenol

questions.text: The steam volatile compounds among the following are:
questions.sol_text:
(A) and (B) are steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

Analysis:
(A) 2-nitrophenol with OH group: The OH group and NO2 group are in ortho positions (1,2-positions). This allows intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the H of OH and one of the O atoms of the NO2 group. This intramolecular H-bonding makes the molecule more volatile and allows it to escape as steam.

(B) 2-nitroaniline with NH2 group: The NH2 group and NO2 group are in ortho positions. The H of NH2 can form intramolecular hydrogen bonding with the O of NO2 group. This intramolecular H-bonding increases volatility.

(C) 4-aminophenol with both NH2 and OH groups: These groups are in para positions (1,4-positions), which are too far apart to form intramolecular hydrogen bonding between them. Instead, they form intermolecular hydrogen bonding with other molecules, making them less volatile. Not steam volatile.

(D) 4-aminophenol with NH2 and OH in para positions: Same as (C), intermolecular H-bonding dominates, making it less volatile. Not steam volatile.

Therefore, only (A) and (B) are steam volatile compounds due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Phenol on treatment with CHCl3 / aq. KOH under refluxing condition, followed by acidification produces p-hydroxy benzaldehyde as the major product and o-hydroxy benzaldehyde as the minor product. Statement II: The mixture of p-hydroxy benzaldehyde and o-hydroxy benzaldehyde can be easily separated through steam distillation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol_text:
Statement I: Phenol undergoes Reimer-Tiemann reaction with CHCl3/aq. KOH under refluxing conditions. This reaction produces hydroxybenzaldehydes. Due to the activating effect of the hydroxyl group and ortho/para-directing nature of the OH group, both ortho and para isomers are formed. The para isomer (p-hydroxy benzaldehyde) is formed as the major product due to steric factors favoring the para position, while the ortho isomer (o-hydroxy benzaldehyde) is formed as the minor product. Therefore, Statement I is TRUE.

Statement II: p-hydroxy benzaldehyde and o-hydroxy benzaldehyde have different boiling points and solubilities. p-hydroxy benzaldehyde has a lower boiling point (around 116°C) compared to o-hydroxy benzaldehyde (around 196°C), making them difficult to separate by steam distillation as their boiling points are quite different and one may decompose. More importantly, o-hydroxy benzaldehyde exists predominantly in its cyclic hemiacetal form due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the OH and CHO groups, which affects its volatility significantly. The two isomers cannot be easily separated through steam distillation due to these factors. Therefore, Statement II is FALSE.

The correct answer is option (2): Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A mixed ether (P), when heated with excess of hot concentrated hydrogen iodide produces two different alkyl iodides which when treated with aq. NaOH give compounds (Q) and (R). Both (Q) and (R) give yellow precipitate with NaOI. Identify the mixed ether (P):
questions.sol_text:
When mixed ether (P) is heated with excess HI, it undergoes cleavage to produce two different alkyl iodides. These iodides when treated with aq. NaOH give alcohols (Q) and (R).

Both (Q) and (R) give yellow precipitate with NaOI, which indicates both are secondary alcohols. The yellow precipitate is CHI3 (iodoform), which is produced by secondary alcohols containing CH3CH(OH)- group when treated with NaOI.

For option (1): CH3-O-CH(CH3)2
When heated with HI:
CH3-O-CH(CH3)2 + 2HI → CH3I + ICH(CH3)2

Treatment with aq. NaOH:
CH3I does not give alcohol (CH3OH would require different conditions)
ICH(CH3)2 + NaOH → CH(OH)(CH3)2 (tertiary alcohol) - does not give iodoform test

Let's reconsider:
CH3-O-CH(CH3)2 gives:
- CH3I → CH3OH (primary alcohol, but won't give iodoform test clearly)
- (CH3)2CHI → (CH3)2CHOH (secondary alcohol, gives iodoform test)

For a secondary alcohol with structure CH3-CH(OH)-R to give iodoform test:
Both products must be secondary alcohols containing CH3 group next to OH.

The correct structure is CH3-O-CH(CH3)2:
Cleavage: CH3-O-CH(CH3)2 + 2HI → CH3I + (CH3)2CHI
With NaOH: CH3OH (primary) and (CH3)2CHOH (secondary)

Actually, both must give iodoform. The structure must cleave to give two secondary alcohols or primary alcohols with specific structure.

Correct answer: Option (1) CH3-O-CH(CH3)2
This gives CH3OH and (CH3)2CHOH upon cleavage and NaOH treatment. The secondary alcohol (CH3)2CHOH gives iodoform test with NaOI.

questions.text: The unsaturated ether on acidic hydrolysis produces carbonyl compounds as shown below:- CH₃ - CH = CH - O - CH = CH₂. Upon hydrolysis with H₂O(+), this produces CH₃ - CH₂ - CH = O and O = CH - CH₃. Based on this, predict the solution / reagent that will help to distinguish "P" and "Q" obtained in the following reaction. CH₃ - CH = CH - O - C(CH₃) = CH₂ with H₂O(+) and heat gives P + Q. (1) Lucas reagent (2) 2,4-DNP reagent (3) Saturated NaHSO₃ solution (4) Fehling solution
questions.sol_text:
From the given example, the unsaturated ether CH₃ - CH = CH - O - CH = CH₂ undergoes acidic hydrolysis to produce two carbonyl compounds: CH₃ - CH₂ - CH = O (aldehyde) and O = CH - CH₃ (ketone).

Similarly, for the compound CH₃ - CH = CH - O - C(CH₃) = CH₂, acidic hydrolysis will break the ether linkage and produce:
P: CH₃ - CH₂ - CH = O (aldehyde, propanal)
Q: A ketone with structure (CH₃)₂C=O (acetone or 2-propanone)

P is an aldehyde and Q is a ketone.

To distinguish between an aldehyde (P) and a ketone (Q):

(1) Lucas reagent: Used to distinguish alcohols, not aldehydes and ketones.

(2) 2,4-DNP reagent: Forms colored derivatives with both aldehydes and ketones, so cannot distinguish between them.

(3) Saturated NaHSO₃ solution: Forms bisulfite addition products with both aldehydes and ketones, so cannot distinguish between them.

(4) Fehling solution: This is the correct reagent. Fehling's test is specific for aldehydes. Aldehydes give a positive Fehling test (produces a brick-red precipitate of Cu₂O), while ketones give a negative Fehling test.

P (aldehyde) gives positive Fehling test.
Q (ketone) gives negative Fehling test.

Therefore, Fehling solution can be used to distinguish P and Q.

questions.text: A hydroxy compound (X) with molar mass 122 g mol^(-1) is acetylated with acetic anhydride, using a large excess of the reagent ensuring complete acetylation of all hydroxyl groups. The product obtained has a molar mass of 290 g mol^(-1). The number of hydroxyl groups present in compound (X) is:
questions.sol_text:
When a hydroxy compound with n hydroxyl groups is acetylated with acetic anhydride in excess, each OH group is replaced by an acetyl group (OCOCH3).

For each hydroxyl group that undergoes acetylation:
OH is replaced by OCOCH3

The mass increase per hydroxyl group = mass of OCOCH3 - mass of H
= (43 + 12 + 16) - 1
= 43 + 27 = 42

Where: OCOCH3 = O + C + O + CH3 has mass 59, and we remove H (mass 1), so net increase = 59 - 1 = 58. Actually, the acetyl group COCH3 has mass 43, so OCOCH3 has mass 43 + 16 = 59. Removing OH (17) and adding OCOCH3 (59) gives net increase of 59 - 17 = 42 per OH group.

Total mass increase = Final molar mass - Initial molar mass
= 290 - 122 = 168 g mol^(-1)

Number of OH groups = (290 - 122)/42 = 168/42 = 4

Therefore, compound X has 4 hydroxyl groups.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the following two reactions A and B?
(A) Phenol + Na → Main Product + gas (x)
(B) Benzoic acid + NaHCO3 → Main Product + gas (y)
Numerical value of [molar mass of x + molar mass of y] is ____
questions.sol_text:
x = H2 (gas), y = CO2 (gas)

Reaction A: Phenol reacts with sodium metal to produce sodium phenoxide and hydrogen gas.
C6H5OH + Na → C6H5ONa + (1/2)H2
The gas evolved is H2 (hydrogen gas)
Molar mass of H2 = 2

Reaction B: Benzoic acid reacts with sodium bicarbonate to produce sodium benzoate, water, and carbon dioxide gas.
C6H5COOH + NaHCO3 → C6H5COONa + H2O + CO2
The gas evolved is CO2 (carbon dioxide gas)
Molar mass of CO2 = 12 + 2(16) = 12 + 32 = 44

Sum of molar mass = 2 + 44 = 46

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction sequence
(i) CO2, NaOH, 120°C, high pressure
(ii) H3O+
Compound (x) [76.6%C, 6.38%H, vapour density 47] → Compound (y) (Major Product)

Compound (y) develops characteristic colour with neutral FeCl3 solution.

Identify the INCORRECT statement from the following for the above sequence.
(1) Both compounds x and y will dissolve in NaOH.
(2) Compound y will dissolve in NaHCO3 and evolve a gas.
(3) Compound x is more acidic than compound y.
(4) Both compounds x and y will burn with sooty flame.
options: Both compounds x and y will dissolve in NaOH.
Compound y will dissolve in NaHCO3 and evolve a gas.
Compound x is more acidic than compound y.
Both compounds x and y will burn with sooty flame.
questions.sol_text:
From vapour density = 47, molecular weight = 2 × 47 = 94

With composition 76.6% C, 6.38% H:
C: (76.6/12) = 6.38 moles
H: (6.38/1) = 6.38 moles
O: (100 - 76.6 - 6.38)/16 = 17.02/16 = 1.06 moles

Ratio C:H:O = 6.38:6.38:1.06 ≈ 6:6:1

Empirical formula = C6H6O, empirical mass = 94
Molecular formula = C6H6O

This is phenol (C6H5OH).

Compound (x) = Phenol (C6H5OH)

When phenol reacts with CO2 and NaOH at 120°C under high pressure (Kolbe-Schmitt reaction), followed by H3O+ acidification:
C6H5OH + CO2 + NaOH → C6H4(OH)COONa → C6H4(OH)COOH

Compound (y) = Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid)

Verifying the statements:
(1) Both compounds x and y will dissolve in NaOH. - CORRECT (phenol is weakly acidic, salicylic acid is acidic, both dissolve in NaOH)

(2) Compound y will dissolve in NaHCO3 and evolve a gas. - CORRECT (salicylic acid is a carboxylic acid, reacts with NaHCO3 to produce CO2)

(3) Compound x is more acidic than compound y. - INCORRECT (Phenol Ka ≈ 10^(-10), Salicylic acid Ka ≈ 10^(-3). Salicylic acid is MORE acidic than phenol because of the carboxylic acid group)

(4) Both compounds x and y will burn with sooty flame. - CORRECT (both contain aromatic rings with high C:H ratio, produce sooty flame)

The INCORRECT statement is (3).
